 2                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

 3   resolution by Senator Griffo, mourning the 

 4   untimely death of Oneida County Sheriff's Deputy 

 5   Kurt Wyman on Tuesday, June 7, 2011.

 6                THE PRESIDENT:   Senator Griffo.

 7                SENATOR GRIFFO:   Thank you, 

 8   Mr. President.  I rise today in sadness to 

 9   remember, memorialize and to pay tribute to a 

10   young police officer, a 24-year-old individual by 

11   the name of Kurt Wyman.  

12                Kurt Wyman was an outstanding 

13   individual.  He was a young man of courage, of 

14   valor, a caring family man of integrity and 

15   character with a deep-rooted faith.  

16                Deputy Sheriff Wyman graduated from 

17   high school in 2005.  And he had true concern and 

18   passion for our country and his community, so out 

19   of high school he joined the United States Marine 

20   Corps Reserves, and in 2008 he was activated and 

21   saw duty in Iraq, serving his country with 

22   distinction and honor.

23                When he came home from the military, 

24   he decided that he wanted to continued to serve 

25   his community and applied and was accepted into 

                                                                5112

 1   the Oneida County Sheriff's Department.  And in 

 2   2007 he became a deputy sheriff.  

 3                During his four years as a police 

 4   officer in the County of Oneida, where he served 

 5   and protected the community each and every day, 

 6   he received a number of recognitions and 

 7   accolades.  He was a Rookie of the Year, and he 

 8   received the Grand Cordon Medal, which is a medal 

 9   that recognizes outstanding achievement by a 

10   detail in law enforcement at the Department of 

11   Sheriff.

12                This young man truly was making a 

13   difference in the community.  He was full of 

14   life, and he was a genuine, sincere, 

15   compassionate individual who wanted to do what 

16   was best for his family and to continue to do 

17   what he could to serve his community.

18                On the night of June 6th and over 

19   the morning hours of June 7, 2011, he was called 

20   to a domestic disturbance.  A standoff occurred, 

21   and during that period he was shot and killed.

22                He leaves behind a wife by the name 

23   of Lauren who, when you look at stories such as 

24   this that are so tragic, but it becomes more 

25   intensified that on the very night that he was 

                                                                5113

 1   shot, when she learned of the news, she went into 

 2   labor.  So at the same time that they were trying 

 3   to save Deputy Sheriff Wyman's life, his wife was 

 4   delivering his daughter.

 5                He died; he leaves two children, 

 6   Alexander and Adyson, and loving parents, 

 7   Lynnette and Brian Wyman.  Today we rise to 

 8   continue to just know that we will pray for his 

 9   soul and for his family.  

10                We offer our condolences to the 

11   Department of Sheriff in Oneida County and to all 

12   the residents of Oneida County, today and always, 

13   as a result of this loss.

 1                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

 2   Resolution Number 2562, by Senator Perkins, 

 3   mourning the death of Gilbert Scott-Heron, an 

 4   American poet, musician and author.  

 5                "WHEREAS, It is the custom of this 

 6   Legislative Body to pay tribute to citizens of 

 7   the State of New York whose lifework and civic 

 8   endeavor serve to enhance the quality of life in 

 9   their communities and the great State of New 

10   York; and 

11                "WHEREAS, Gilbert Scott-Heron of 

12   Harlem, New York, died on Friday, May 27, 2011, 

13   at the age of 62; and 

14                "WHEREAS, Gilbert 'Gil' Scott-Heron 

15   was born on April 1, 1949, in Chicago, Illinois, 

16   to Bobbie Scott-Heron and Gil Heron; and 

17                "WHEREAS, Gilbert Scott-Heron's 

18   mother sang with the New York Oratorio Society, 

19   and his father, nicknamed 'The Black Arrow,' was 

20   a soccer player who in the 1950s became the first 

21   black athlete to play for the Glasgow Celtic 

22   Football Club in Scotland; and 

23                "WHEREAS, Gilbert Scott-Heron was a 

24   long-time resident of Harlem, New York.  He was 

25   an American poet, musician, and author known 

                                                                5116

 1   primarily for his work as a spoken-word 

 2   performer; and 

 3                "WHEREAS, When Gilbert Scott-Heron 

 4   was 12 years old, he moved with his mother to the 

 5   Bronx and enrolled in DeWitt Clinton High 

 6   School.  Soon thereafter, he was granted a full 

 7   scholarship to the Fieldston School; and 

 8                "WHEREAS, After high school, Gilbert 

 9   Scott-Heron attended Lincoln University in 

10   Pennsylvania, as it was the college chosen by his 

11   biggest Langston Hughes; and 

12                "WHEREAS, After about two years at 

13   Lincoln University, Gilbert Scott-Heron took a 

14   year off to write his novels; and 

15                "WHEREAS, Although Gilbert 

16   Scott-Heron never received his undergraduate 

17   degree, he received a master's degree in creative 

18   writing in 1972 from John Hopkins University.  

19   His 1972 dissertation was titled 'Circle of 

20   Stone'; and 

21                "WHEREAS, Gilbert Scott-Heron began 

22   his recording career in 1970 with the LP 'Small 

23   Talk at 125th and Lenox.'  The album's 15 tracks 

24   dealt with themes such as the superficiality of 

25   television and mass consumerism, and the 

                                                                5117

 1   difficulties faced by inner-city residents; and 

 2                "WHEREAS, Gilbert Scott-Heron's 

 3   poetic style has been influential upon every 

 4   generation of hip hop music since his popularity 

 5   began.  As such, he has been described by music 

 6   writers as 'the godfather of rap' and 'the black 

 7   Bob Dylan'; and 

 8                "WHEREAS, Armed with a humanistic 

 9   Spirit and imbued with a sense of compassion, 

10   Gilbert Scott-Heron leaves behind a legacy which 

11   will long endure the passage of time and will 

12   remain as a comforting memory to all he served 

13   and befriended; now, therefore, be it 

14                "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

15   Body pause in its deliberations to mourn the 

16   death of Gilbert Scott-Heron, an American poet, 

17   musician, and author; and it be further 

18                "RESOLVED, That a copy of this 

19   resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to 

20   the family of Gilbert Scott-Heron."

25                You know, on May 27th we lost one of

 1   the greatest musicians and poets, at least in my 

 2   time.  At the young age of 62, Gil Scott-Heron 

 3   passed away.  And for those of us who have been 

 4   touched by his work, there will forever be a void 

 5   in our hearts.  

 6                He began his recording career in 

 7   1970 with the LP "Small Talk at 125th and 

 8   Lenox."  The album's 15 tracks dealt with themes 

 9   such as the superficiality of television and mass 

10   consumerism, the hypocrisy that was so prevalent 

11   at the time, and his most famous lyrics came from 

12   a song called "The Revolution will Not be 

13   Televised."  

14                Some of the lyrics from the album's 

15   opening tracks are as follows:  

16                "The revolution will not be brought 

17   to you by the Schaefer Award Theatre and will not 

18   star Natalie Wood and Steve McQueen or Bullwinkle 

19   and Julia.  The revolution will not give your 

20   mouth sex appeal.  The revolution will not get 

21   rid of the nubs.  The revolution will not make 

22   you look five pounds thinner, because the 

23   revolution will not be televised, Brother."

24                Gil's poetic style has been 

25   influential upon every generation of hip hop 

                                                                5119

 1   music since his popularity began, though he 

 2   himself said he did not want to take 

 3   responsibility for it -- somewhat of a 

 4   left-handed criticism.  As such, he has been 

 5   described by music writers as "the godfather of 

 6   rap" and "the black Bob Dylan."  

 7                Gil will be sorely missed, yet he 

 8   leaves behind a legacy that will long endure the 

 9   passage of time and will remain a comforting 

10   memory to all those he befriend and affected with 

11   his work.  

12                Gil was a good friend of mine, and 

13   we had a friendship that included competing 

14   against each other in basketball.  He wasn't as 

15   good as me, needless to say.  But nevertheless, 

16   you know, in his last days in the neighborhood, 

17   it was sad to see such a genius in a very 

18   difficult circumstance in terms of his health.  

19                But again, I think the most 

20   important thing about him is the legacy of the 

21   work that he has left behind that is still 

22   influencing many that have come after him.  

23                So thank you very much.
